$description: The platform-neutral contract every generator (Web now, Android/iOS later) must satisfy. Restates design-system/platform-mapping.md's conventions in a form the design-to-code pipeline itself can be validated against. Android and iOS are NOT implemented this phase — this file only makes the shared JSON structurally suitable for them later.

visualParityRule.rule: Web, Android, and iOS use the same semantic visual system. Platform-native UI implementation is allowed (each platform renders with its own toolkit — Tailwind/CSS on Web, Jetpack Compose on Android, SwiftUI on iOS), but visual semantics must remain equivalent across all three. No platform may independently choose a different visual identity.
mustBeTheSameAcrossPlatforms: colors — every color a screen shows must resolve from shared/tokens.json#/color/semantic (light and dark), never a platform-local palette
background hierarchy — the same background.primary/background.secondary/surface.default/surface.elevated/surface.variant layering, in the same relative order of lightness
typography hierarchy — the same shared/typography.json scale and weight relationships (display/heading/body/label/caption), even though the concrete unit differs (rem vs sp vs Dynamic-Type pt)
spacing scale — the same shared/spacing.json 4px-based step values, converted to the platform's fixed layout unit (px/dp/pt), never a platform-invented scale
radius family — the same shared/shape.json radius steps mapped to the same component types (e.g. radius.large for all cards on every platform)
surface hierarchy — the same card/panel/sheet elevation relationships from shared/elevation.json

component intent — the same shared/components.json recipes (e.g. PrimaryButton, CourseCard, Checkout) resolve to the same token references regardless of platform; only the rendering technology changes
artwork system — the same shared/artwork.json 5-motif course-artwork composition (gradient + icon + category chip), never a platform-specific illustration style
platformNativeDifferencesAllowed: native navigation mechanics — e.g. Android back-stack/gesture nav, iOS swipe-back, Web browser history — the navigation MODEL is native, the navigation SURFACE'S color/typography/spacing is not
platform-safe-area behavior — status bar / notch / home-indicator insets are platform-native concerns with no Web equivalent

native interaction affordances — e.g. Android ripple, iOS haptic feedback / press-scale, Web :hover — the interaction MECHANISM is native, the resulting state color (hover/pressed containers from shared/tokens.json) is not

native control behavior where required by platform convention — e.g. a native iOS date/time picker sheet, an Android native Snackbar host — as long as the control's own visible colors/typography still resolve from the shared semantic tokens, not a platform default theme
explicitlyNotAllowed: an independent Android color palette (e.g. Material You dynamic color) replacing shared/tokens.json's semantic colors
an independent iOS color palette (e.g. raw UIColor system colors) replacing shared/tokens.json's semantic colors
separate auth (Login/Register) styling that diverges from the same background/surface/card treatment used elsewhere on that platform
a separate CourseCard identity per platform — artwork motifs, category chip treatment, and card surface must be recognizably the same component everywhere

unrelated dark/light systems — dark mode on every platform must be the same semantic structure re-resolved (shared/tokens.json#/color/semantic/dark), never a platform-specific dark palette invented independently
visualParityRule.enforcementToday: No Android/iOS code exists yet (still NOT IMPLEMENTED, see android/ios sections below) — this rule governs how that future code must be generated from shared/*.json, and is the criterion a future PR review must check against. Today it also re-states why Web's own Login/Register (D51) and Purchase Success/Instructor Dashboard/etc. (D52) corrections were required to consume the SAME shared background/surface tokens as every other Web screen rather than any screen-invented alternative.

pipeline.diagram: Shared JSON (design-to-code/shared/*.json, design-to-code/screens/*.json, design-to-code/patterns/*.json) -> Web generator (tools/design-to-code/generate.js) -> [Android generator later] -> [iOS generator later]
pipeline.rule: A generator READS shared JSON and WRITES platform-specific generated artifacts. A generator never writes back into shared/screens/patterns JSON, and a generated artifact is never hand-edited — regenerate from source instead.

existingWebTokenPipeline.role: Pre-existing, NOT replaced. Reads design-system/design-tokens.json + themes/*.json directly and writes web/styles/tokens.css, web/styles/tailwind-theme.css, web/src/lib/design-tokens.generated.ts. This design-to-code pipeline is a SEPARATE, ADDITIONAL generator for the layers token-pipeline does not cover (component recipes, navigation/shell rules, artwork rules, screen-to-route mapping) — it does not duplicate or conflict with token-pipeline's output.
existingWebTokenPipeline.decisionReference: execution/DECISIONS_LOG.md D35 (token-pipeline's own plain-Node, no-external-dependency precedent, followed by tools/design-to-code/ for the same reason).

consumes: design-to-code/screens/*.json (for route/shell mapping only, not for visual re-generation of full pages)
web.generatesInto: web/src/lib/design-to-code.generated.ts (typed constants: component recipe names, navigation shell rules, artwork motif mapping, responsive breakpoint re-export for JS-side consumers that can't read a CSS var)
web.colorConvention: CSS custom property, kebab-case, theme-scoped via [data-theme] — already generated by tools/token-pipeline/generate.js; this pipeline's TS constants REFERENCE the same var names, never redefine them.
web.doesNotGenerate: Raw CSS custom properties for tokens — that remains token-pipeline's job. This pipeline generates the layer ABOVE raw tokens: named recipes and structural constants.

android.status: NOT IMPLEMENTED — mapping only, for future readiness.
android.wouldGenerateInto: android/app/src/main/java/.../design/MentoraTokens.kt (or equivalent) — a MentoraTheme Compose theme object exposing colors/typography/spacing/shape/elevation via CompositionLocal, plus component-recipe data classes mirroring shared/components.json's structure 1:1.
readinessNotes: shared/tokens.json's dot-path names already match platform-mapping.md's documented Android naming convention 1:1 — a generator only needs a dot-path -> camelCase transform, already implemented once in tools/token-pipeline/generate.js's kebabPath()/camelToKebabSegment() helpers (inverse direction needed for Android/iOS, not yet written).

shared/components.json's token references (e.g. "color.brand.primary") resolve identically regardless of target platform — no Android-specific re-authoring of component recipes is anticipated, only a new renderer for the same recipe data.

shared/navigation.json's shell definitions are Web-shaped (Sidebar/Navbar) since Instructor/Admin are Web-only by product design (product/USER_ROLES.md) — an Android app (Student-only surfaces) would consume shared/navigation.json#/shells/coursePlayerShell and a new, not-yet-specified MobileBottomNavigation-driven shell, not Sidebar/Navbar.

colorSchemeMapping.$description: Every dot-path in shared/tokens.json#/color/semantic mapped to its Jetpack Compose Material 3 ColorScheme slot, for BOTH light and dark — the generator's job is filling these slots from the SAME resolved values already in tokens.json, never choosing new ones (e.g. never Material You dynamic color).

light.text.link: ColorScheme.primary (rendered as a clickable AnnotatedString span, not a separate slot)
light.success.default/container/onSuccess/onSu: custom ColorScheme extension (M3 has no built-in success role) — extend MaterialTheme via a CompositionLocal, same pattern web uses for --color-success-*
light.warning.*: custom ColorScheme extension, same reasoning as success
light.info.*: custom ColorScheme extension, same reasoning as success

colorSchemeMapping.dark: Same slot mapping as light — Compose's darkColorScheme(...) is filled from shared/tokens.json#/color/semantic/dark's values for the identical slot names above. No slot is ever re-mapped between light/dark; only the resolved value differs, per the Layer-1/Layer-2/Layer-3 rule shared/tokens.json itself documents.

shapeMapping.$description: shared/shape.json radius steps -> Compose Shapes slots.
shapeMapping.radius.large: Shapes.medium (cards, dashboard cards, all cards per shared/shape.json)
shapeMapping.radius.xlarge: Shapes.large (dialogs, bottom sheets — top corners only, via a custom RoundedCornerShape not Shapes.extraLarge's all-corner default)
shapeMapping.radius.full: CircleShape / RoundedCornerShape(percent = 50) (chips, badges, avatar, progress bar, switch)

android.elevationMapping: shared/elevation.json's e1-e4 shadow values map to Compose `tonalElevation`/`shadowElevation` Dp values on Surface/Card composables — per the design system's own 'borders over shadow' principle (see visualParityRule above), Compose cards should prefer a `border` stroke (BorderStroke(1.dp, ColorScheme.outlineVariant)) with LOW tonalElevation, not a heavy shadowElevation, to visually match Web's subtle e1/e2 shadows rather than Material's default elevated-card shadow weight.

ios.status: NOT IMPLEMENTED — mapping only, for future readiness.
ios.wouldGenerateInto: ios/Mentora/Design/MentoraTokens.swift + a Color Set asset catalog (Any/Dark appearances) generated from shared/tokens.json#/color/semantic — mirrors design-system/platform-mapping.md § 9's suggested repository structure.
readinessNotes: Typography must wrap each token in a Dynamic-Type-aware Font style per shared/tokens.json#/units — the shared JSON already carries the base fontSize/lineHeight numbers a SwiftUI generator needs; it does not yet carry an explicit Dynamic-Type category mapping (inferred to be a straightforward relative-scale wrap, not a new value set).

shared/components.json's `select` recipe explicitly maps to a Menu/Picker-style SwiftUI control (design-system/COMPONENTS.md § Select, Native mapping) — already documented, no additional shared-JSON change needed to support it later.

shared/artwork.json's motif system is platform-agnostic (gradient + icon + chip composition) and requires no iOS-specific restructuring — only a new SwiftUI view implementing the same composition recipe.

colorMapping.$description: Every dot-path in shared/tokens.json#/color/semantic mapped to a Color Set asset name (Any Appearance = light values, Dark Appearance = dark values, generated into ONE asset per dot-path so SwiftUI's automatic dark-mode resolution does the theme switch, mirroring Web's [data-theme] and Android's ColorScheme — never a manually-branched `if colorScheme == .dark` in view code).
colorMapping.assetNamingConvention: mentora<PascalCase dot-path>, e.g. background.primary -> mentoraBackgroundPrimary, brand.primaryContainer -> mentoraBrandPrimaryContainer
colorMapping.swiftAccessorConvention: Color.mentora<PascalCase>, e.g. Color.mentoraBrandPrimary, generated as a Color extension reading the asset catalog entry above — the SAME name for every dot-path in the semantic table (background.*, surface.*, text.*, border.*, brand.*, secondary.*, accent.*, success.*, warning.*, error.*, info.*, overlay.*).
colorMapping.systemColorRule: Never substitute a raw UIKit/SwiftUI system color (Color.gray, Color(.systemBackground), etc.) for a semantic token slot — every one of the dot-paths above must resolve through its mentora-prefixed asset, per explicitlyNotAllowed above.

typographyMapping.$description: shared/typography.json scale -> SwiftUI Font styles, each wrapped for Dynamic Type via `.font(.mentora<Name>)` custom Font extensions rather than raw `.system(size:)` calls.
typographyMapping.caption: Font.mentoraCaption (relativeTo: .caption)

shapeMapping.$description: shared/shape.json radius steps -> SwiftUI shape values.
shapeMapping.radius.medium: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12) — buttons, inputs, select, snackbar, menus
shapeMapping.radius.large: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16) — course card, dashboard card, all cards
shapeMapping.radius.xlarge: UnevenRoundedRectangle (top corners only, 24pt) — dialog / bottom sheet
shapeMapping.radius.full: Capsule() — chip, badge, avatar (Circle() when 1:1), progress bar

ios.elevationMapping: shared/elevation.json's e1-e4 map to a `.mentoraElevation(_:)` ViewModifier applying `.shadow(color:radius:y:)` tuned to the SAME subtle rgba/blur/offset values Web's e1-e4 use — per the 'borders over shadow' principle, pair every elevated Card view with a `.overlay(RoundedRectangle(...).stroke(Color.mentoraBorderDefault, lineWidth: 1))` rather than relying on shadow weight alone, matching shared/components.json's card recipe (border + subtle shadow, not shadow-only).

generatorFailureContract.rule: Generation MUST fail loudly (non-zero exit, printed reason) rather than emit partial/guessed output when: a screen references a component name absent from shared/components.json; a component/screen references a token dot-path absent from shared/tokens.json (or shared/typography|spacing|shape|elevation.json); two screens declare the same screenId; a pattern is referenced by a screen but does not exist under design-to-code/patterns/.
generatorFailureContract.implementedBy: tools/design-to-code/validate.js — see design-to-code/validation/EXTRACTION_REPORT.md and MAPPING_REPORT.md for what it actually checks and found.
